newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank says oil service industry healthier.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank says oil service industry healthier.

text.p: Leading Swiss private bank Union Bancaire Privee said on Wednesday the oil service industry was coming back to life for fund managers after 15 years of "disastrous" stock performance.

In its latest survey of market trends, the bank said the industry now enjoyed strong fundamentals, rising prices and high demand after a period of excess capacity and business decline due to a collapse in oil prices between 1983 and 1985.
"During this period...companies had to adapt in order to survive. Nowadays, a tougher generation of profitable companies is emerging in a much more rational environment," it said.
"Within the industry, offshore drilling in general, and deep-water offshore-drilling in particular, are enjoying the most exciting fundamentals."

The bank, recommending U.S. oil services firms Schlumberger and Reading & Bates as well as Transocean Offshore for more aggressive investors, said it expected corporate earnings in the oil service industry to benefit from an improving environment as demand growth translates into rising capacity utilisation.
This should improve the earnings visibility, said the bank, which specialises in private and institutional asset management.
